criteria.scenario: A newer UI guidance source recommends behavior that conflicts with an accepted internal UDR based on a frozen 2026-09-30 corpus. A maintainer wants to edit the old evidence statement in place so all projects immediately use the new recommendation.
criteria.decision_to_make: Govern the conflict, freshness and supersession without silently rewriting provenance.
must_do: register the new source with date/scope
preserve the old claim/decision
compare scope/method/authority before supersession
use explicit supersedes/deprecated links when warranted
inspect affected downstream decisions/evals and keep project-local overrides separate
must_not_do: overwrite the old evidence in place
assume newer publication date automatically wins
claim external specialist depth if the asset was not actually reviewed

criteria.scenario: A billing team has a prose rule: one monthly SMS per child/per period should go to every unique eligible guardian number, including when the amount is zero. Legacy supplies contact relationships; Finance decides billing eligibility; an operator must approve a mass send. A developer wants to implement directly from the prose and write tests afterward. No concrete examples, boundary cases or counterexamples have been agreed.
criteria.decision_to_make: Decide whether the behavior is implementation-ready and define the smallest pre-implementation executable contract needed before coding.
must_do: distinguish business rule, concrete example, implementation and executed test evidence
create at least one concrete representative example with actors/data/trigger/expected result before implementation
include material boundary or counterexamples such as duplicate guardian numbers, zero amount, missing eligible recipient or approval refusal
keep unresolved business questions explicit instead of inventing policy
choose an executable oracle/layer and preserve stable rule/example traceability into acceptance, tests/evals and later production observation
must_not_do: declare G3 ready from prose alone
implement first and rewrite examples afterward to match the code
encode a queue/provider/transport architecture into business acceptance without evidence that it is a constraint

criteria.scenario: An AI agent named Reviewer is instructed in its prompt to be read-only. In practice it can read repositories, execute arbitrary shell commands, query production records containing personal data, and its environment exposes a production database write credential. The external model/provider data-handling policy has not been verified.
criteria.decision_to_make: Define the security/governance boundary and the controls required before this agent can be used on the intended production-support workflow.
must_do: state that persona or prompt text is not an authorization boundary
classify the personal/production data and verify model/provider compatibility before sending it
define an explicit agent capability matrix and remove or deny unnecessary production-write capability
apply least privilege to credentials/tools and bound sensitive tool output or egress
require enforceable approval for consequential actions where risk warrants it and preserve audit evidence
must_not_do: treat the word Reviewer or a read-only prompt as an enforceable control
send restricted or sensitive data to an unverified provider by default
leave a production write credential available merely because the agent is instructed not to use it

criteria.stage_name: Feedback → next iteration — Production Learning Loop
criteria.scenario: A new billing-eligibility calculation passed all pre-release tests and the deployment is operationally healthy. In production, operators repeatedly override the automated result for a small set of families and support notes mention special guardianship changes. The team proposes a hard-coded exception patch. The original product outcome has not yet been measured.
criteria.decision_to_make: Decide how to interpret the production mismatch, what must be learned or changed, and what evidence is required before claiming the loop is closed.
must_do: reopen the expected rule/example/outcome and capture the production observation with version/population/time scope
describe and classify the expected-vs-observed delta before assuming it is a code defect
investigate what operators know or decide that the system does not, including domain/data/requirement possibilities
propagate supported learning to every affected model/example/decision/test/eval/knowledge or observability artifact and re-verify changed contracts
keep HEALTHY distinct from SUCCESSFUL and record Definition of Value as unverified until outcome evidence exists
must_not_do: equate green tests or healthy deployment with product success
hard-code the observed exception without investigating whether the explicit model or source-of-truth assumptions changed
rewrite expected behavior post hoc to match production without evidence and supersession
